title: Check role-code separation for the pinned two-contact BIT product
body:
All six unordered pairs of the four roles interfere at port zero. The uniform independent-root alphabet has size at most one. Its retained singleton still leaks in the adjoint, and the fixed unpruned signed tariff fails by more than 4.668 million at the first trial.

## Scope and source

Credits aliromman and the exact d018f6c peer source in the archive. The priced test applies to the unpruned two-contact word with optimistic helper credits. The complete source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit-two-contact-role-alphabet/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. `python3 -I -B verify.py` passed the cold 16-block native impulse/adjoint tests, the independent reference and all listed corruption controls. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Check a port-dependent code or a new amortized paid schedule with changed ownership and cleanup.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
